inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-06-30), 138.5m. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and Cummins funds the flat count with buybacks (resumed 2026 after a 2023-25 pause for Meritor deleveraging).
inputs.cash_note: Cash and equivalents 3,179 + current marketable securities 745 at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q XBRL MarketableSecuritiesCurrent).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back via Metrics.csv StockBasedComp (93m). Equity-award withholding tax not separately tagged in XBRL (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation absent); immaterial at <0.3% of revenue, so no top-up.
inputs.interest_income_note: Net DEBT company (net debt 2,964m), so interest income is not stripped; the flows are unlevered (built from EBITDA), so interest expense is charged once via net debt in the bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: H1 2026 repurchases 468m (Q1 243m); zero in FY2023-FY2025. Repurchaser: the flat count is being funded.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.8%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.0% at ~6% debt/EV weight (6.9bn debt vs ~73bn market cap) -> WACC ~9.4%, rounded to 9.0% because cyclicality is priced in the scenario flows (bear includes a post-pre-buy truck trough) and must not be charged again in the rate. Same WACC in all three scenarios (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost already sits inside operating expenses and hence inside EBITDA; operating lease liabilities (562m at FY2025) excluded from net debt. Treatment (B), charged once; no separate lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows include 100% of Cummins India (~51% owned) and other consolidated JVs. NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at ~20x FY2025 NCI earnings (114m) = 2,280m, above the 1,059m book value because Cummins India trades at a large premium to book. Flows are NOT made attributable-only.
inputs.jv_treatment: Company-defined EBITDA includes equity income from unconsolidated JVs (469m FY2025, 302m H1 2026, mostly China/India). Only the distributed portion is cash, so the EBITDA margin path is company EBITDA + SBC add-back less ~0.45pp of retained JV earnings. No separate JV stake in the bridge (its income is in the flows).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF with cyclical adaptations (routing row: US cyclical industrial). Cummins is an operating manufacturer/distributor whose value is its free cash flow; no bank/REIT/holdco features. Cyclicality handled in the FLOWS: FY2026 guidance year (revenue +10-13%, company EBITDA 18.0-18.5%) followed by an EPA-2027 pre-buy in FY2027 and a truck-demand air pocket in FY2028 in every scenario, with terminal margins set at a mid-cycle level rather than the FY2026-27 peak, and a 12-15x terminal cap. FY0 = FY2025 (revenue 33,670). Reported FY2025 FCF 2,386; FY2024 FCF 279 was depressed by the ~1.9bn EPA emissions settlement payment and FY2022 by Meritor integration working capital, so the FCF CAGRs are noise. FY2025 net income includes 458m of Accelera electrolyzer charges (415m non-cash). Base year-1 owner-FCF margin ~9% vs TTM reported FCF of ~3.4bn (8.9% of TTM revenue) plus after-tax interest -- consistent. No filings extracted to text (XBRL-only ticker); anchors from SEC companyfacts and Metrics.csv.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests (Cummins India et al.) at ~20x FY2025 NCI earnings

historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (interest income not stripped; net debt). FY2020->FY2025 owner FCF 2,164 -> 2,293 (+1.2%/yr) and FY2022->FY2025 1,013 -> 2,293 (+31%/yr) are both artefacts: FY2022 trough (Meritor acquisition working capital), FY2024 279 (EPA settlement ~1.9bn). SBC is ~0.3% of revenue so owner and reported CAGRs barely differ. Revenue 5yr CAGR includes the Meritor acquisition (Aug-2022) and the 2024 Atmus split-off (removes filtration revenue from FY2024 on). Equity 5yr CAGR 9.0% sits within 30% of revenue (11.2%) and EPS (11.3%), so no divergence flag. EPS FY2023 (5.19, EPA settlement charge) and FY2024 (28.55, Atmus split-off gain) are distorted; the endpoints used are not.

base.rationale: FY2026 at guidance midpoint (+11.5%, company EBITDA 18.25% -> 18.1% on the adj ex-retained-JV basis). FY2027 EPA pre-buy + data-center power; FY2028 truck air pocket (-3%, margin -1.3pp on deleverage). Revenue reaches ~43.8bn in FY2030, below management's raised 45-50bn target; mid-cycle margin 18.8% vs management's >20% 2030 target. Capex above D&A through the large-engine capacity build. WC capture negative (manufacturer: receivables + inventory exceed payables, ~20% of revenue).

scenario_narratives.base: Power Systems keeps compounding on hyperscale/AI standby and prime power (generators, natural-gas gensets, BESS) while Distribution/aftermarket grows with the installed base. North American heavy-duty truck gets a modest EPA-2027 pre-buy in FY2027 and pays for it with a FY2028 air pocket; China on/off-highway recovers slowly. Accelera losses shrink after the electrolyzer exit. Revenue lands at ~44bn by 2030 (just short of the 45-50bn target) and EBITDA settles at a mid-cycle ~19% (company basis), not the >20% management targets.
scenario_narratives.bull: Data-center power demand stays structural through the decade and the large-engine capacity expansion fills; the EPA-2027 rule holds and triggers a full pre-buy, with HELM/X10 content gains; the post-pre-buy dip is shallow because Power Systems and aftermarket carry the mix. Cummins hits the top of its raised 2030 targets (~49bn revenue, >20% EBITDA) and buybacks continue.
scenario_narratives.bear: Hyperscaler capex digests after 2027 and Power Systems backlog normalises, just as the EPA-2027 NOx rule is delayed or diluted -- no pre-buy, and a freight recession plus Section 232 tariffs push FY2028 NA truck and construction volumes down ~10% with operating deleverage to ~14.5% EBITDA. PACCAR/OEM in-sourcing erodes engine share; margins recover only to ~16%, roughly the pre-data-center mid-cycle.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (up from the 15% default): FY2026 is a guided-up, near-peak year with the thesis concentrated in one end-market (AI data-center capex) and a regulatory-timed truck cycle, but the balance sheet (net debt ~0.5x EBITDA) carries no solvency risk. Base 50%: management has raised guidance three times this year and the base still sits below its 2030 targets. Bull 30% (down from 35%): needs both sustained hyperscaler capex AND an intact EPA-2027 pre-buy -- two independent things.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cyclical industrial valued on unlevered owner FCF built from components, with the truck cycle (pre-buy then air pocket) explicit in every scenario and mid-cycle terminal margins capped at 12-15x terminal FCF. Risk is charged in the flows and scenario weights, not stacked in the discount rate. SBC is immaterial (~0.3% of revenue), so the house/street band is narrow.
key_risks_to_valuation: Hyperscaler/AI data-center capex slowdown hitting the highest-margin segment (Power Systems)
EPA 2027 NOx rule delay/reversal removing the pre-buy
North American freight/construction downturn and Section 232 tariffs
OEM engine in-sourcing (PACCAR) and customer concentration
Retained JV earnings (China/India) not converting to cash; NCI valued at a multiple, not book
Warranty exposure on new HELM/X10 platforms (accrual 2.8bn)
